Do employees living in Liechtenstein who return home daily (or expect 45 or fewer non-return days) still have to answer denomination, spouse employment and all the child questions? D-007 says Liechtenstein residents get all the source tax questions. But the AC-05.7.3 examples show '–' for denomination and children in the 'in principle no source tax' rows, and for those people the answers feed no tariff code. Under G-01 we should not ask them. This decides whether the Liechtenstein daily-return questions come before the rest of the source tax block and close it early.

After submission HR may change an answer so that new questions apply. Examples: a move from Switzerland to Germany, a corrected nationality, a marriage. The employee was never asked denomination, children or the cross-border questions, so the tariff code cannot be 're-derived from the latest answers' (D-037). Who supplies the missing answers? Does the employee's questionnaire reopen for just those questions, or is it all HR-side? And what is recorded for HR in the meantime: no tariff code, or an 'incomplete' state?

Should the Zurich calculator's logic (tariff letters, church-tax Y/N) be used for every employee subject to source tax, including those living in other Swiss cantons (for example Aargau or St. Gallen)? Or only for Zurich residents and cross-border commuters? If other cantons' residents need their own canton's rules or church-tax rules, the tariff computation and possibly the denomination question change.

The Germany and Liechtenstein non-return-day questions say 'in the calendar year'. For someone who starts in, say, November, is that the rest of the current year, the projected full year, or the next year? The answer changes what the question text says and when a later change (by HR) is needed.

Can the employee leave the questionnaire and come back later to finish it (a saved draft)? Or must it be completed in one session? D-036 only says answers are kept 'while the employee goes back and forth'. Is there a deadline (for example before the first working day), and what happens to an unsubmitted draft?

"the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child" - Prescribes the UI interaction (add/remove repeating blocks). The business need is only that every child is assessed; how the employee enters several children is an engineering/UX choice.

"Notes | Flow step 6, child block repeated per child (employee can add further children). Expressions describe one child." - 'Child block repeated' and 'Expressions' describe a form or rule-engine implementation rather than a business need.

"It is recorded for HR, together with the decision whether the source tax questions apply." - Says what intermediate derived state to store. Whether 'source tax questions apply' is kept as its own recorded value is a design choice; HR's stated need is the liability result and the tariff code.

"Rows marked inferred were not observed in the calculator and must be checked (OQ-calculator-coverage). Expression describes one child." - 'Expression' is rule-engine wording that slips implementation thinking into the business rule description.

info.message: Are there limits on the dates an employee can enter? For example: a first working day in the past or far in the future, a date of birth that makes the employee under age or implausibly old, or a spouse's date of birth in the future. Should the questionnaire reject these or just accept them?

HR 'provides the wording' for the permit reminder. Who delivers the final text before the build, and is it one fixed English text for Muster AG? Or must each customer company be able to set its own wording?

D-007 says Lonio 'shows' the Liechtenstein result. Does the employee see any derived result (tariff code, 'in principle no source tax liability', insurance start date) at the end of the questionnaire? Or is it only recorded for HR? The email copy explicitly excludes derived results, which suggests the employee does not see them.

The copy contains sensitive data (religion, children, custody) and goes to any address the employee types in. Is that acceptable without checking the address (for example typing it twice or confirming it)? Does 'answers exactly as submitted, nothing more' still allow the question texts and section headings, so the copy can be read?

AC-01.2.1 says every address part, including the country, is required. But in its example table the Switzerland row shows '–' for country where the Germany row shows 'required'. Is this just a mistake in the table, or is the country meant to default to Switzerland?

Should the questionnaire explain 'of age and in first education' and 'replacement income' (for example age limits, what counts as first education, which benefits count)? Or does the employee judge these alone, as in the calculator? Wrong self-assessment changes the tariff code.

For married employees and registered partners the children question also covers the spouse's or partner's children. For a stepchild, how should the employee answer the custody and 'common household with the other parent' questions, given that the 'other parent' is not the spouse? Is the calculator's wording reused as it is?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: What does Pensionskasse Muster expect in 'Canton' for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and lists only Swiss cantons; employees abroad cannot be registered without an answer.
options: Canton of work (Zurich) for employees abroad
Canton of residence; the fund gives a rule for employees abroad
Canton means work canton for everyone
open_questions.recommendation: Provisionally ask only residents of Switzerland (D-002); verify with a domain expert and the fund.

open_questions.question: How does the pension fund want registered partnerships and separated employees registered (the list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), and does it want partner details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A wrong civil status or a missing partner date of birth makes the registration wrong.
options: Keep provisional mapping (both as Married with spouse/partner date of birth)
open_questions.recommendation: Use the provisional mapping (D-003) until a domain expert verifies it.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's screen ask for a spouse's date of birth (or other data) for Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screenshots show only Single and Married; a hidden required field would block registration.
options: Extra field shown - add a question
open_questions.recommendation: Do not ask divorced/widowed employees (D-004); verify with a screenshot of the fund's screen.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the calculator on paths not explored: residence block for A/B/H tariffs, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and the child paths marked 'inferred' in the child result table?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result; an unverified path could produce a wrong tariff code.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live

open_questions.question: Is the email address for the copy kept after the copy has been sent, and is it recorded for HR, or used only for sending?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No receiving party needs the address; keeping it would hold personal data no party needs (data minimisation).
options: Use it only to send the copy, do not keep it
Keep it and record it for HR
open_questions.recommendation: Use it only to send the copy and do not record it for any receiving party.

questions.question: Do employees living in Liechtenstein who return home daily (or expect 45 or fewer non-return days) still have to answer denomination, spouse employment and all the child questions? D-007 says Liechtenstein residents get all the source tax questions. But the AC-05.7.3 examples show '–' for denomination and children in the 'in principle no source tax' rows, and for those people the answers feed no tariff code. Under G-01 we should not ask them. This decides whether the Liechtenstein daily-return questions come before the rest of the source tax block and close it early.

After submission HR may change an answer so that new questions apply. Examples: a move from Switzerland to Germany, a corrected nationality, a marriage. The employee was never asked denomination, children or the cross-border questions, so the tariff code cannot be 're-derived from the latest answers' (D-037). Who supplies the missing answers? Does the employee's questionnaire reopen for just those questions, or is it all HR-side? And what is recorded for HR in the meantime: no tariff code, or an 'incomplete' state?

Should the Zurich calculator's logic (tariff letters, church-tax Y/N) be used for every employee subject to source tax, including those living in other Swiss cantons (for example Aargau or St. Gallen)? Or only for Zurich residents and cross-border commuters? If other cantons' residents need their own canton's rules or church-tax rules, the tariff computation and possibly the denomination question change.

The Germany and Liechtenstein non-return-day questions say 'in the calendar year'. For someone who starts in, say, November, is that the rest of the current year, the projected full year, or the next year? The answer changes what the question text says and when a later change (by HR) is needed.

Can the employee leave the questionnaire and come back later to finish it (a saved draft)? Or must it be completed in one session? D-036 only says answers are kept 'while the employee goes back and forth'. Is there a deadline (for example before the first working day), and what happens to an unsubmitted draft?

Are there limits on the dates an employee can enter? For example: a first working day in the past or far in the future, a date of birth that makes the employee under age or implausibly old, or a spouse's date of birth in the future. Should the questionnaire reject these or just accept them?

HR 'provides the wording' for the permit reminder. Who delivers the final text before the build, and is it one fixed English text for Muster AG? Or must each customer company be able to set its own wording?

D-007 says Lonio 'shows' the Liechtenstein result. Does the employee see any derived result (tariff code, 'in principle no source tax liability', insurance start date) at the end of the questionnaire? Or is it only recorded for HR? The email copy explicitly excludes derived results, which suggests the employee does not see them.

The copy contains sensitive data (religion, children, custody) and goes to any address the employee types in. Is that acceptable without checking the address (for example typing it twice or confirming it)? Does 'answers exactly as submitted, nothing more' still allow the question texts and section headings, so the copy can be read?

AC-01.2.1 says every address part, including the country, is required. But in its example table the Switzerland row shows '–' for country where the Germany row shows 'required'. Is this just a mistake in the table, or is the country meant to default to Switzerland?

Should the questionnaire explain 'of age and in first education' and 'replacement income' (for example age limits, what counts as first education, which benefits count)? Or does the employee judge these alone, as in the calculator? Wrong self-assessment changes the tariff code.

For married employees and registered partners the children question also covers the spouse's or partner's children. For a stepchild, how should the employee answer the custody and 'common household with the other parent' questions, given that the 'other parent' is not the spouse? Is the calculator's wording reused as it is?

tech_leaks.quote: the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child
tech_leaks.why: Prescribes the UI interaction (add/remove repeating blocks). The business need is only that every child is assessed; how the employee enters several children is an engineering/UX choice.

tech_leaks.quote: Notes | Flow step 6, child block repeated per child (employee can add further children). Expressions describe one child.
tech_leaks.why: 'Child block repeated' and 'Expressions' describe a form or rule-engine implementation rather than a business need.

tech_leaks.quote: It is recorded for HR, together with the decision whether the source tax questions apply.
tech_leaks.why: Says what intermediate derived state to store. Whether 'source tax questions apply' is kept as its own recorded value is a design choice; HR's stated need is the liability result and the tariff code.

tech_leaks.quote: Rows marked inferred were not observed in the calculator and must be checked (OQ-calculator-coverage). Expression describes one child.
tech_leaks.why: 'Expression' is rule-engine wording that slips implementation thinking into the business rule description.

review.summary: Not ready, but close. All examples pass and the open questions are non-blocking. Three things block release. Decision D-036 has new evidence from the email-copy update and must be re-confirmed (error). Five dev-refinement questions are rated major; one shows a contradiction between D-007 and the AC-05.7.3 examples, and another shows a gap in D-037 when HR edits after submission. Several rules and stories cite facts outside their cited set; one row (separated → spouse date of birth) disagrees with D-003. After that, the main open items are the inferred child-tariff paths and four places where implementation wording leaks into the spec.

findings.title: D-036 has new evidence and must be re-confirmed
findings.why: This is the only error-level check. Five new email-copy facts touch D-036 (answers kept while the employee goes back and forth, and what gets submitted). Release can't happen while a decision is out of date against its evidence.
findings.evidence: decisions error on D-036: new facts F-hr_email_copy-029105, -37cede, -ab2538 and 2 more
findings.action: Re-check D-036 against the copy-email facts. Update the decision if it should also cover the copy, then run `pipeline reconfirm D-036`.

findings.title: Liechtenstein daily commuters: D-007 contradicts the AC-05.7.3 examples
findings.why: D-007 asks Liechtenstein residents every source tax question. But the examples show '–' for denomination and children in the 'in principle no source tax' rows. Under G-01, asking them would collect data that feeds no tariff code. This also decides the order of the source tax questions.
findings.action: Add a decision: ask the Liechtenstein daily-return and 45-day questions first, and close the source tax section early when there is in principle no liability. Then align D-007 and the AC-05.7.3 examples.

findings.title: HR edits after submission can open questions that were never answered
findings.why: D-037 says results are 're-derived from the latest answers'. But if HR changes residence, nationality or civil status, answers the result depends on (denomination, children, cross-border) were never collected. The tariff result is then undefined.
findings.action: Decide who supplies the missing answers: the questionnaire reopens for just those questions, or HR enters them. Also decide what HR sees in the meantime (an 'incomplete' status vs no tariff code). Record it in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Scope: is the Zurich calculator logic used for residents of other cantons?
findings.why: Most staff are in Zurich, but residents of Aargau, St. Gallen and other cantons may need their own canton's church-tax rules or tariff rules. That would change the tariff computation and possibly the denomination question.
findings.action: Confirm with HR or a domain expert. Either record that the Zurich logic applies to all (Muster AG's tax office is Zurich), or exclude other cantons and add that to the exclusions.

findings.title: Some rules and stories cite facts outside their cited set; one row disagrees with D-003
findings.why: Some rows have no backing. One is a real content conflict: the Separated row in pension_fund_civil_status includes the spouse's date of birth, but D-003 says separated employees are entered as Married without it.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: rule.pension_fund_civil_status; rule.single_parent_h_tariff (c78e0c); rule.cross_border_tariff_applies (bc1639, 52b67a); rule.source_tax_result (b6d9b3); US-04.3/05.4/06.1/08.1 (d7431e, b6d9b3); US-08.3 (Julia incident); 'H tariff' purpose on 8 child items
findings.action: Fix the Separated row to match D-003/D-004, or update D-003. Add the missing fact refs to the cited sets. Add a cited fact or decision behind the 'H tariff' purpose of the child items.

findings.title: Inferred child-tariff paths have not been checked against the calculator
findings.why: Lonio now owns the tariff result. About 15 example rows in US-06.2–06.5 are marked 'inferred, to verify', and US-06.4 extends a rule to divorced and widowed employees without a source. A wrong path gives HR a wrong tariff code.
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage (D-009); inferred stories US-06.2, US-06.3, US-06.5, US-06.6; trace_judge US-06.2/06.3/06.4
findings.action: Keep domain-expert verification as a stated go-live condition. Ideally run the inferred paths through the calculator now and replace 'inferred' with observed facts.

findings.title: Non-return days 'in the calendar year' are unclear for employees who start mid-year
findings.why: The answer, and possibly the question text, depends on which period counts. Without a rule, employees starting in, say, November will answer inconsistently, and the cross-border tariff may be wrong.
findings.action: Clarify with a domain expert which period applies: rest of the year, projected full year, or next year. Record a decision and adjust the question wording.

findings.title: Saving an unfinished questionnaire and finishing deadline not defined
findings.why: This affects how D-036 retention works, reminders, and what happens before the first working day. Engineering can't size the flow without it.
findings.action: Decide whether the employee can save and come back later, whether there is a deadline (e.g. before the first working day), and what happens to an unsubmitted questionnaire. Fold this into the D-036 re-confirmation.

findings.title: Implementation wording in the spec
findings.why: Phrases like 'repeating child block', 'add/remove', 'Expressions' and storing 'source tax questions apply' as its own value prescribe UI or storage design instead of the business need.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: US-06.1, feature.md notes, US-04.3, information.md
findings.action: Rephrase as needs: 'each child is assessed separately'. Drop the 'Expression' wording and drop recording the intermediate 'questions apply' value.

findings.title: Smaller gaps to tidy up
findings.why: These cause rework during refinement if left open.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement: AC-01.2.1 table shows '–' for country in the Switzerland row; US-08.4 has no check on the copy address and the copy holds sensitive data; US-08.1 has no owner for the permit-reminder wording; coverage: F-pension_portal-3a97ab unused
findings.action: Correct the AC-01.2.1 table. Decide on confirming the copy address and whether the copy includes question texts. Name who supplies the reminder text. Cite F-pension_portal-3a97ab in US-02.2 as the reason for the mid-month rule.
